details.text: No registered surveyor mid-span clearance measurements provided. Vertical clearances to driveways, parking areas, and site features cannot be calculated without pole locations and conductor elevation data.

details.text: Site plan and electrical plan show overhead electric lines (labeled OHE) but provide no dimension annotations. Complete absence of clearance dimensions throughout plan set makes verification impossible.

runComments.comment: Site plan and electrical plan show overhead electric lines (labeled OHE) but provide no dimension annotations showing clearances from site features to these lines. The requirement mandates that all clearance dimensions originate from the outside conductor, not from the pole centerline. The complete absence of clearance dimension annotations renders verification impossible. Additionally, no notation specifies whether dimensions are measured from the outside conductor or pole center.

While overhead electric lines are shown on the site plan, grading plan, and landscape plan as linear routing, NO clearance dimensions are shown anywhere in the plan set—neither from outside conductor nor from pole centerline. This makes it impossible to determine whether any clearance dimensions that do exist are measured correctly from the outside conductor (as required) or incorrectly from pole center. However, the fundamental issue is that clearance dimensions are entirely absent, making this specific verification unnecessary because there are no dimensions to evaluate for correctness. The absence of any clearance dimensions throughout the plan set is the primary deficiency (covered under other items).

comments.headline: Trees—species and clearances not utility-compatible
comments.summary: Landscape plan shows mitigation trees near overhead electric lines with species including Live Oak and Cedar Elm. These species exceed utility-compatible height limits and lack documented lateral clearance distances from conductors (50 feet for transmission; 10 feet for distribution).

details.text: Landscape plan shows mitigation trees ('M' designation) near southern property boundary where overhead electric lines exist. Plant list specifies 2 Live Oak (mature height 60+ feet) and 10 Cedar Elm (mature height 40-60 feet). Live Oak and tall Cedar Elm exceed utility-compatible height thresholds. Trees within 10 lateral feet of distribution lines must be from ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible list with mature heights ≤20 feet. No lateral distance dimensions shown from trees to overhead conductors.

runComments.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows mitigation trees marked 'M' positioned within close proximity to overhead electric lines (OHE) at the southern boundary. Proposed shade trees and ornamental trees are listed on Sheet 35 (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) but the specific location of each tree species on the landscape plan is not cross-referenced with clearance distance callouts. Without species identification on the landscape plan for each tree near overhead lines and without explicit verification that such trees are from the ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible list, compliance cannot be confirmed. Additionally, no lateral distance dimensions are provided from tree locations to overhead conductors.

Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows mitigation trees ('M' designation) and other plantings near the overhead electric line shown along the southern boundary of the site. Tree list (Sheet 32) provides caliper sizes and species. However, no lateral distance dimensions are shown on the landscape plan indicating how far proposed trees are located from the overhead electric conductors. Per UCM § 1.10.10.4, trees must maintain 50 lateral feet from transmission conductors (or 10 lateral feet from distribution conductors if facility is distribution rather than transmission). Tree species must be verified against ECM Appendix F 'UC' (Utility Compatible) designation for trees within the clearance zones. Applicant must provide: (1) dimension callouts showing lateral distances from OHE to all trees within 50 feet of the line; (2) confirmation that tree species are from the UC list; (3) site grading contours showing clearance compliance.

Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows mitigation trees (marked 'M') proposed along southern property boundary near OHE lines. Plant list (Sheet 35) specifies: 2 Live Oak (Quercus virginiana) and 10 Cedar Elm (Ulmus crassifolia). Live Oak is not utility-compatible (mature height 60+ feet exceeds UC list criteria); Cedar Elm (mature height 40-60 feet) is problematic near distribution lines. Trees within 10 lateral feet of distribution lines must be from ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible list with mature heights ≤20 feet generally.

Buildings 1 and 2 are positioned near western property boundary in proximity to these ROW-adjacent electric facilities. No clearance dimensions shown indicating distance from building faces to outside conductor of overhead lines in the adjacent ROW.

runComments.comment: Overhead electric lines exist in the right-of-way (Valley View Road, western boundary). Buildings are proposed near this ROW. However, no clearance dimensions or surveyed conductor elevations are provided to verify that both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances are maintained from existing or relocated facilities.

Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) shows overhead utility poles located outside the western property line in the Valley View Road right-of-way, with overhead lines running along the road and extending onto the property. Buildings 1 and 2 are positioned near the western property boundary in proximity to these ROW-adjacent electric facilities. However, no clearance dimensions are shown on site plan indicating the distance from building faces to the outside conductor of the overhead lines in the adjacent ROW. Applicant must provide dimension callouts on site plan and building elevations showing the 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearances are maintained from ROW-located overhead electric facilities to all buildings.

Overhead electric lines shown on site plan along southern boundary adjacent to Buildings 6, 7, 8. No surveyed conductor elevations or clearance dimension annotations provided to verify 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance requirement is met.

comments.headline: Utility equipment and infrastructure—clearance documentation missing
comments.summary: Trash enclosures, water meters, water lines, decorative lighting, electric meters, transformers, and service masts lack clearance documentation from overhead electric facilities. Meter access clearances and equipment installation details are not verified.
comments.attn: Meter access clearance verification incomplete (EL-1.38); transformer niche installation applicability unclear (EL-1.44); secondary/primary crossing angle unclear (EL-1.33); water meter coordination (EL-1.28).

details.text: Landscape plan may show site lighting fixtures but clearance verification dimensions and relocation notes relative to overhead electric lines are not provided. No photometric plan with clearance dimension callouts provided if decorative lighting proposed beneath overhead facilities.

runComments.comment: Landscape plan may show site lighting/decorative fixtures but clearance verification dimensions and relocation notes relative to overhead electric lines are not provided. Without explicit clearance dimension annotations showing 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances from conductors to lighting fixtures, or notes indicating relocation of fixtures away from overhead lines, compliance cannot be verified.

Site plan references exterior lighting requirements (Block 1, Sheet 9) and notes that all exterior lighting must be full cut-off and fully shielded per Subchapter E 2.5. However, no photometric plan or lighting fixture location plan is provided showing specific decorative fixture locations in relation to the overhead electric lines documented on the site. If decorative lighting is proposed beneath or in proximity to overhead lines, clearance dimensions (7.5-foot sky-to-ground, 15-foot radial) must be provided. Applicant should clarify whether decorative lighting fixtures are proposed beneath overhead facilities and if so, provide photometric plan with clearance dimension callouts or relocation confirmation.
Landscape plan shows site lighting but specific decorative lighting locations relative to overhead lines are not clearly identified or dimensioned. Clearance verification dimensions not provided.

comments.headline: Construction phase clearances and safety requirements
comments.summary: Construction staging areas and equipment laydown zones are not documented on a logistics plan. Additionally, the required Texas law 48-hour safety notification to Austin Energy is not prominently placed on cover sheets in the standard required format.
comments.attn: Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003 requires explicit notification language on contract documents.

details.text: Construction staging areas and equipment zones are shown on erosion control plan but no documentation verifies that these areas maintain required 10-foot radial clearance from overhead electric lines. This is a construction-phase requirement distinct from permanent clearances.

runComments.comment: Construction staging areas and equipment zones are shown on the erosion control plan, but no documentation verifies that these areas maintain the required 10-foot radial clearance from overhead electric lines. This is a construction-phase requirement distinct from permanent clearances. Without explicit dimension annotations or notes, compliance cannot be confirmed.

Sheet 3 documents extensive construction coordination requirements for work near transmission facilities, referencing OSHA clearance requirements. However, no construction staging area plan, equipment laydown zone diagram, or work platform logistics plan is provided with the site plan submittal. During construction, equipment and materials must maintain 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead lines per OSHA 1910.333 and UCM § 1.10.2 (this is distinct from permanent clearance requirements). Applicant must provide a detailed construction logistics plan showing staging areas, equipment operation zones, crane swing radius, and scaffold/platform locations with dimension callouts verifying 10-foot radial clearance from all overhead electric facilities during construction phases.

No construction staging plan or logistics plan provided showing staging area boundaries, crane swing radius, or material storage locations relative to overhead electric lines. Cannot verify 10-foot radial clearance during construction from submitted documents.

details.text: Sheet 3 contains transmission-specific safety meeting note but does not include the required standard 48-hour notification language mandated by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003 in a standard location (cover sheet or general notes). Applicant must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines.

runComments.comment: Sheet 3 (General Notes) contains a note stating that a pre-construction safety meeting is required with Austin Energy 48 hours before commencement of construction (Electric Transmission Notes, Item 3). However, this is a transmission-specific note. The required standard note for all projects with overhead high-voltage lines per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003, stating that the owner/contractor must NOTIFY Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines, is not present in a standard location (cover sheet or general notes) in the standard required format. The current note references a safety meeting but does not include the explicit 48-hour notification requirement language mandated by Texas law.
